newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Three more Pakistani ministers to be sworn in.
newsitem.headline: Three more Pakistani ministers to be sworn in.

text.p: Three more ministers were due to join Pakistan's new caretaker cabinet on Wednesday after failing to reach Islamabad in time for the main oathtaking ceremony, a government official said.
He said President Farooq Leghari would swear in Fakhruddin Ebrahim as Justice Minister, as well as Abdullah Memon and Abdul Hayee Baloch whose portfolios had not yet been assigned.
The caretaker cabinet, led by Meraj Khalid, 80, took office on Tuesday after Leghari sacked the government of Benazir Bhutto for alleged corruption, nepotism and misrule.
Leghari said the cabinet would be in office for only 90 days until a general election called for February 3.

Sahibzada Yaqoob Khan was made Foreign Minister, a post he has held twice before. The Defence Ministry went to Shahid Hamid, Leghari's lawyer. Omar Afridi became Interior Minister, responsible for Narcotics Control, Federal Investigation, States and Frontier Regions, and Kashmir Affairs.

Syeda Abida Hussain, a former information minister and ambassador to the United States, took the education, science and technology portfolio. She is the only cabinet member from the main opposition Pakistan Moslem League led by Nawaz Sharif.
Shafqat Mahmood, a member of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party, became Minister of Food, Agriculture and Livestock.
Irshad Haqqani, a journalist, took over the Information Ministry, while the Ministry of Industries and Production went to Pakistan's top taxpayer, Sadiq Awan, a businessman.
Zubair Khan, brother-in-law of Leghari, was made Commerce Minister. Javed Burki, currently a vice-president of the World Bank, was expected to join the cabinet as finance minister.
